tools.name: get_coverage_stats
tools.description:
Live coverage of the ERC-8004 agent economy across Base and Ethereum.

Returns counts only: how many agents are indexed, how many expose a live MCP server / OpenAPI / well-known card, total MCP tools and OpenAPI methods observed, contracts verified, EOAs and owners identified, plus a per-chain breakdown. No names, addresses, or handles. Use this to size the market and see where capability density is growing.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/market` (x402, USDC on base-mainnet) returns the full capability market map — which capabilities are saturated vs open, per-capability agent lists, and momentum. Every response from this free tool carries an `unlock` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: get_leaderboards
tools.description:
ERC-8004 agents by ladder step, by advertised tool and method counts, and most recently indexed.

Ranked lists — by four-step ladder position, by MCP tool count, by OpenAPI method count (what an agent lists, not what it can do), and most-recently indexed — each with agent_id, chain, public name, a shareable detail URL, and the relevant count. Names and counts only: no owner wallets, handles, or endpoint URLs.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/trending` (x402, USDC on base-mainnet) returns trending intel — top earners, fastest-rising agents, and integration candidates ranked with the signals behind the ranking. Every response from this free tool carries an `unlock` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: get_agent_summary
tools.description:
Objective, counts-only signals for one ERC-8004 agent.

Args (BOTH OPTIONAL — call with `{}` to see Agent Zero itself):
    chain: one of "base", "ethereum". Default: "base".
    agent_id: the numeric ERC-8004 agent id. Default: 19353 (Agent Zero, the agent serving this MCP endpoint).
Example: `{}` returns Agent Zero on base; `{"chain": "base", "agent_id": 19353}` is the explicit form.

Returns reachability, TLS validity, x402 support, payments to the agent's own address (booleans only: payments_to_agent_address, payment_attribution; payments_to_owner_wallet and payments_received are deprecated, removed 2026-12-05), MCP tool count, OpenAPI method count, well-known presence, owner-named (boolean), and a neutral status label (status_label_v2: Reachable, payment signals / Reachable, no payment signals / Stub or unreachable; the old status_label is deprecated, sunset 2026-11-07). No owner identity string and no payment amounts — those are paid. Returns an `error` field if the agent is not indexed. Use this to vet a counterparty agent before transacting.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/agent/{agent_id}?chain={chain}` (x402, USDC on base-mainnet) unlocks trust_verdict (safe_to_transact / caution / avoid / insufficient_data), readiness_score, Sybil-adjusted reputation, the reviews-from-paid-jobs (commerce-backed) breakdown, and for Transact-ready or higher agents a plain-English `brief` (due-diligence summary from our data, with sources and as-of date) — the decision-driving values this free response returns as `null` inside a `locked` map. Every response carries an `unlock` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: get_address_record
tools.description:
What we can see about one x402 pay-to address on Base: how many registrations name it, whether they share one owner, which registration its payments are credited to, and x402 payments seen (count and USDC, all time and 30 days).

Facts only. Base only; only x402 settlements visible in USDC transfer logs; a payment shows money reached the address, not which service was bought. The registrations listed name the address in their own files; that is not a statement about who controls it.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/address/base/{address}` (x402, $0.01 USDC, the same price as the single-agent lookup) returns the full record with the registration list and payer breakdown. The `next_step` block carries the exact URL and price.

tools.name: get_network_teaser
tools.description:
A capped teaser of the graph of transfers between agent operator wallets.

Returns connected agents (nodes) and the USDC/ETH transferred between their operator wallets (edges; transfers, not confirmed purchases), capped to a small connected sample (≤200 nodes). This is a truncated preview, not the full network. Use it to see which operator wallets send value to which.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/graph` (x402, USDC on base-mainnet) returns the operator-wallet transfer graph, capped to the top 2,000 agents by payment value plus the edges among them (USDC/ETH amounts; filters chain, min_usd, limit; meta.truncated). Every response from this free tool carries an `unlock` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: agent_trust_teaser
tools.description:
Credit-score-style TEASER for one ERC-8004 agent's trust profile.

Args (BOTH OPTIONAL — call with `{}` to see Agent Zero itself):
    chain: one of "base", "ethereum". Default: "base".
    agent_id: the numeric ERC-8004 agent id. Default: 19353 (Agent Zero, the agent serving this MCP endpoint).
Example: `{}` returns Agent Zero on base; `{"chain": "base", "agent_id": 19353}` is the explicit form.

By construction returns ONLY: name, chain, agent_id, public ladder_step / ladder_name (the four-step ladder; readiness_bucket is deprecated), and a 1-line verdict headline. Agents that belong to a platform registering many agents and have no endpoint or activity of their own yet also carry `platform_listed: true` and `platform`. Every decision-driving value — trust_verdict, readiness_score, risk_flags, money-flow details, counterparty list, full score breakdown — is redacted as `null` and enumerated in the `locked` map. The response carries the exact paid endpoint URL (/v1/intel/agent/{agent_id}?chain={chain}), the x402 price as currently configured, and a one-line how-to-pay-via-x402 hint. Returns `error` with the same unlock pointer if the agent is not indexed, so a caller probing an unknown id still sees how to pay for a known one.

Paid counterpart: `GET /v1/intel/agent/{agent_id}?chain={chain}` (x402, USDC on base-mainnet) returns the full trust verdict (safe_to_transact / caution / avoid / insufficient_data), readiness_score + sub-scores, Sybil-adjusted reputation, and the reviews-from-paid-jobs (commerce-backed) breakdown, and for Transact-ready or higher agents a plain-English `brief` (sources and as-of date included). Every response from this free tool carries an `unlock` + `paid_upgrade` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: list_payable_x402_endpoints
tools.description:
Directory of ERC-8004 agents that answered a well-formed HTTP 402 x402 challenge during our last field probe. OBSERVATION ONLY — not a score, ranking, or endorsement.

Args (ALL OPTIONAL — call with `{}` for the top 10 across both chains):
    chain: one of "base", "ethereum" (omit for both). Default: null.
    limit: 1..10 rows (free-tier cap). Default: 10.
Returns per-row raw probe facts: agent_id, chain, endpoint_url, http_402_ok, network, asset, price_usd as the challenge advertised, payTo_present (boolean — the actual address is paid), sibling_agent_ids (other ERC-8004 ids served by the same gateway row — the 'shared operator' cue), probed_at. Plus `total_endpoints_valid_402` and `total_agents_valid_402` so a caller can see what fraction of the surface this free slice covers.

Source: the 0946 field-test one-shot probe (unauthenticated, read-only, no payment signed). See the `field_test_url` field for the full writeup.

Paid counterpart: the paid x402 /v1/intel/* endpoints return the same-origin enriched intel on any single agent in this list — owner identity, payment history, peers, trust verdict, Sybil-adjusted reputation. Every response from this free tool carries an `unlock` + `paid_upgrade` block with the exact paid endpoint, price, and payment discovery.

tools.name: check_x402_endpoint
tools.description:
Find out if agents can actually pay you. Free check of an x402 seller endpoint (Seller Check). Sends only unpaid requests: confirms the route answers HTTP 402, reads the challenge (header and body, v1 or v2), checks every accepts entry (scheme, network, asset, amount, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds, and extra.name/extra.version against the token's real EIP-712 domain), the named payment service's /supported, and /pricing, /openapi.json, /.well-known/x402 for consistency.

Args:
    url: https URL of the paid route (required).
    method: "GET" or "POST" (optional; default from the seller's OpenAPI file, else GET).
    body: optional JSON body for POST routes (max 8 KB).
Returns checked_at, overall (pass|warn|fail) and checks[] with status, reason and a fix hint. Never pays. Limits: 10 checks per caller per hour, 3 per host per hour.

tools.name: seller_check
tools.description:
Find out if agents can actually pay you. PAID ($0.50 USDC on Base, x402) Seller Check: an independent test of an x402 seller endpoint. Runs the free checks, then makes one real paid call to the seller (only if the seller's price is at most $0.10) and returns a report with every check, both transaction links, pass/warn/fail, findings and fix hints. One free re-run within 7 days.

Payment: call once without payment to get the x402 v2 requirements (returned as `payment_required`), then repeat the call with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2) or X-PAYMENT (v1) header on this MCP HTTP request. The same service is POST https://api.onchainagentintel.io/v1/seller-check.

Args:
    url: https URL of the paid route (required).
    method: "GET" or "POST" (optional).
    body: optional JSON body for the paid call (else the seller's own example; we never invent data).
    route: optional path to test on the url's host.
    contact_email: optional; stored, never published.
    public: true lets the result page be indexed (default private).
